Inspecting and Diagnosing Pipeline Runs

Michael Hallquist & Dan Shallal

23 Oct 2026

Source: vignettes/diagnosing_pipeline.Rmd
diagnosing_pipeline.Rmd

Overview

BrainGnomes separates routine progress inspection, diagnosis, and recovery:

  • inspect_project() answers, “What is happening now?”
  • diagnose_project() answers, “What needs attention, and what evidence is available?”
  • reconcile_project_jobs() checks known allocations for stale tracking records.
  • resolve_project_submission() records a confirmed outcome for one uncertain submission.

Inspection and diagnosis use stored tracking state and saved run evidence by default. An optional read-only inspection refresh can compare active records with the scheduler. Neither inspection nor diagnosis repairs records or submits work. The two recovery functions make changes only when explicitly requested, as described below.

library(BrainGnomes)
scfg <- load_project("/project/my_study")

Both functions also accept the project directory or configuration YAML path directly. If the project root is the current working directory, the input can be omitted:

setwd("/project/my_study")
inspect_project()
diagnose_project() # guided browser in an interactive R session

Automatic discovery checks only the current directory. It does not search parent directories, and reports a clear error if project_config.yaml is not there.

Inspect current project progress

The default inspection integrates all tracked runs:

status <- inspect_project(scfg)
status

The printed dashboard gives overall counts, stage/stream progress, and a bounded list of subjects that are active or need attention. Long tracking fields such as scheduler options, paths, and manifests remain available in the returned object but are not printed automatically.

The object contains ordinary data frames at several resolutions:

status$overview
status$active
status$reconciliation
status$stages
status$subjects
status$subject_stages
status$runs
status$attempts
status$submissions
status$jobs

The same tables are available through summary():

summary(status)                         # one-row overview
summary(status, by = "stage")
summary(status, by = "subject")
summary(status, by = "subject_stage")
summary(status, by = "active")

Because these are data frames, ordinary R queries work without another API:

subset(status$subjects, status != "COMPLETED")
subset(status$subject_stages, sub_id == "540296")
subset(status$jobs, lifecycle_status %in% c("RUNNING", "QUEUED"))

Focus on one subject

Use subject_id with or without the sub- prefix to restrict every resolution, including the run summaries and active-job table:

subject_status <- inspect_project(scfg, subject_id = "540294")
subject_status$overview
subject_status$runs
subject_status$subject_stages
subject_status$active

This is a true inspection scope rather than a display filter, so the returned counts and summaries all describe that subject.

Check active jobs against the scheduler

status$active is available without contacting the scheduler. It reports database status, time in the current state, requested wall time, and flags a running record that has exceeded that request. To compare queued and running database records with their current scheduler states, request a refresh:

refreshed <- inspect_project(scfg, refresh = TRUE)
refreshed$active
refreshed$reconciliation

The refresh is read-only. It preserves the database status, places the scheduler observation beside it, and flags unconfirmed or mismatched records without updating tracking data. Internally this uses the same scheduler query path as wait_for_job(), including the existing Slurm, TORQUE, and local process status functions.

How status is integrated across runs

Each subject/session/stage/stream combination is treated as a logical work unit. Related controller, array, and sentinel jobs are grouped into that unit. For current project status, BrainGnomes uses the newest attempt for every unit rather than the best status ever observed.

Consequently, a successful retry supersedes an older failure, while a failed forced rerun is not hidden by an older success. Work omitted from a later partial retry retains its newest earlier state. Historical attempts remain available in status$attempts and status$runs.

status$submissions also includes submission attempts whose acceptance was never confirmed, even when there is no scheduler job ID or worker log. These are different from jobs that started and failed; an empty $jobs or $failures table alone does not establish that the project is ready to run.

Accepted attempts whose contract/allocation binding is missing or inconsistent are also unconfirmed. Invalid JSON or nonscalar identity metadata is exposed in status$submissions$metadata_error, rather than crashing inspection. Preserve the original evidence and investigate that exact attempt; do not guess its scope to clear a blocker.

The newest logical attempt does not erase an older outstanding allocation. status$active includes older attempts and unconfirmed dependency-blocked or unknown rows; is_current_attempt distinguishes them. If the latest work is complete but an older allocation still lacks termination evidence, the overview reports ACTIVE_PRIOR_ATTEMPTS rather than declaring the project complete.

New tracking timestamps include an explicit UTC designator. Older timestamps without a timezone are interpreted in the current R session’s timezone; BrainGnomes cannot reconstruct a timezone that was never recorded. When reviewing legacy history on a different computer, use the original cluster’s timezone so run ordering remains meaningful, for example:

Sys.setenv(TZ = "America/New_York")
status <- inspect_project(scfg)

Explicit UTC/offset timestamps retain their recorded meaning regardless of this setting. Inspection does not rewrite historical timestamps.

Project-wide inspection describes work represented in the tracking database. It does not invent a status for configured work that has never been submitted.

Interpreting statuses

Raw database statuses are retained in status$jobs$status. Summarized views use friendlier lifecycle labels:

  • COMPLETED: all jobs in the work unit completed.
  • RUNNING: at least one job has started and no failure takes precedence.
  • QUEUED: submitted work has not started.
  • FAILED: the work itself failed.
  • BLOCKED: the database records FAILED_BY_EXT, meaning required upstream work failed.
  • CANCELLED: the work was cancelled.
  • UNKNOWN: the recorded state is missing or unrecognized.

Counts are always retained alongside the convenience status, so mixed states remain visible.

Choose the run you mean

Use the run table to find historical IDs:

status$runs
run_id <- status$runs$run_id[[1L]]

For retry or cancellation, an explicit run ID is safer than "latest" because another submission could become the newest run.

Inspect one run without prompts

Supply "latest" or an explicit ID to restrict every inspection view to one submission:

latest <- inspect_project(scfg, run_id = "latest")
selected <- inspect_project(scfg, run_id = run_id)

selected$overview
selected$subjects
selected$subject_stages
selected$jobs

The older get_project_runs() and get_run_jobs() functions remain as deprecated compatibility wrappers. New code should use $runs and $jobs from inspect_project().

Diagnose failures

Routine monitoring belongs in inspect_project(). When current work has failed, call diagnose_project() from an interactive R session to open the guided dependency and log browser:

diagnose_project(scfg)

When submission issues or a saved preflight report exist, the browser first offers a readiness and recovery review. It can show an uncertain submission even if no scheduler job was recorded. Continuing to tracked jobs shows unresolved failures grouped by stage and stream. A single-job group opens that job directly; a repeated problem first narrows to the affected subjects. Subject, run, and job selections are retained during the drill-down, so the browser never returns to a full run-wide job list unless you explicitly choose that broader view.

If you already know the subject or scheduler job ID, start at that scope:

diagnose_project(scfg, subject_id = "540294")
diagnose_project(scfg, job_id = "66273010")

Scripts, tests, and reports are non-interactive, so the same call returns a structured diagnosis there. Use interactive = FALSE explicitly when you want that result in an interactive R session:

diagnosis <- diagnose_project(scfg, interactive = FALSE)
diagnosis$failures
diagnosis$logs
diagnosis$submission_issues
diagnosis$active_issues
diagnosis$submission_preflight

submission_issues identifies uncertain acceptance, confirmed rejections that have not been superseded, and accepted attempts missing their tracking binding. It includes each attempt’s contract_id, scope, recorded detail, and suggested action. active_issues highlights timing or accounting attention states in the inspection snapshot. To add fresh, read-only scheduler observations, diagnose an inspection returned by inspect_project(scfg, refresh = TRUE).

An existing inspection snapshot can be reused:

diagnosis <- diagnose_project(status, interactive = FALSE)

For a historical post-mortem, select the run explicitly:

diagnosis <- diagnose_project(
  scfg, run_id = run_id, interactive = FALSE
)

Pass interactive = TRUE when code must open the guided browser regardless of how R was started:

diagnose_project(scfg, run_id = run_id, interactive = TRUE)

diagnose_project() is the single diagnosis entry point for both the guided browser and structured, non-interactive results.

Understand automatic submission checks

Calling run_project() again is not a way around an uncertain earlier launch. Every live call checks pending tracking metadata for the selected stages, subjects, sessions, and streams before preparing directories, fingerprinting containers, or submitting setup jobs. Confirmed scheduler failures and cancellations repair stale active records automatically; the console reports which records changed. Active allocations and uncertain acceptance block the relevant request. Neither force = TRUE nor an existing completion marker bypasses these safeguards. Per-submission guards remain in place for launches that race with the initial check.

New tracked submission errors stop the submission loop at the first error instead of repeating a failing launch across the cohort. Scheduler stdout and stderr are retained beside the job manifest. Recognized explicit Slurm policy/request rejections can be corrected and retried; transport errors or lost acknowledgements remain uncertain because a job might have been accepted. This safeguard concerns submission failures, not a guarantee that later worker jobs will succeed.

The check is deliberately lightweight: it reads pending SQLite metadata and batches accounting queries for relevant active jobs. It does not read imaging files, scan output trees, load job manifests, or hash containers. This is a submission-safety check, not full BIDS validation or verification of outputs.

preview <- run_project(scfg, steps = "fmriprep", dry_run = TRUE)
preview$submission_preflight$blockers
preview$submission_preflight$scope_deferred

A dry run returns a plan even when pending metadata indicates blockers. It does not query the scheduler, repair tracking records, or save a preflight report file; a plan with no reported blockers is not a live readiness certificate. debug = TRUE, in contrast, still submits jobs.

For unattended code, the live blocking condition carries the complete report:

# This is a live submission if the check passes, not a preview.
run <- tryCatch(
  run_project(scfg, steps = "fmriprep"),
  bg_submission_preflight_error = function(error) {
    print(error$report$repairs)
    print(error$report$blockers)
    stop(error)
  }
)

An early blocker can stop submission before a new run record exists; use the error’s $report and current diagnosis rather than assuming a new run ID was created. Other submission errors are not necessarily this condition class.

When Flywheel can change the scope

With flywheel_sync, the initial preflight checks project-level setup and controller blockers and labels subject/session scope as deferred. Setup and sync jobs can be submitted after that gate; the provisional local subject list is not certified. After synchronization, the dependent controller discovers the actual scope, including newly arrived subjects or sessions, and repeats preflight before any subject jobs are launched.

The controller saves its assessment to <log_directory>/runs/<run_id>/submission-preflight.json, including when it blocks downstream submission. Read it through the existing workflow APIs:

selected <- inspect_project(scfg, run_id = run_id)
recorded <- selected$submission_preflight
recorded$checked_at
recorded$scope_deferred
recorded$blockers
recorded$repairs

provenance <- get_run_provenance(scfg, run_id)
provenance$submission_preflight

Inspection, diagnosis, and provenance prefer this controller report over the initial assessment when it exists. The original returned run handle may still contain the initial deferred report: read the run again after the controller has executed. A saved report is historical evidence, not current readiness; its blockers remain part of that run’s history after you resolve them. A missing report (NULL) is not proof of readiness either. Use current submission_issues, a refreshed inspection, and the next live preflight to assess unresolved problems. A report read warning or read_error means the saved evidence could not be read, not that the gate passed.

Resolve submission and tracking problems

The exported recovery functions address two different kinds of evidence:

Situation Appropriate action
Known allocation, database still queued/running, scheduler confirms failure or cancellation Preview reconcile_project_jobs(); apply with dry_run = FALSE, or let the next relevant live submission repair it.
Submission is UNKNOWN or SUBMITTING without a confirmed allocation Investigate the exact attempt; use resolve_project_submission() only with confirmed acceptance or rejection evidence.
Confirmed scheduler rejection Correct the request, resources, account, or other rejection cause, then run again. Do not manually declare it accepted.
Scheduler still queued/running Wait, or explicitly cancel when appropriate; do not launch a duplicate.
Accounting is missing/unavailable, or scheduler says completed but tracking remains active Confirm the outcome or verify outputs; these observations do not automatically authorize a retry.

Reconcile a known scheduler job 

# Contacts the scheduler, but does not change SQLite by default.
recovery <- reconcile_project_jobs(scfg)
recovery[, c("job_id", "status", "scheduler_status", "action", "applied")]

After reviewing the observations, explicitly apply confirmed failure or cancellation repairs:

recovery <- reconcile_project_jobs(scfg, dry_run = FALSE)

UPDATE_TERMINAL_FAILURE identifies a proposed terminal repair; applied records whether it was made. CONFIRM_OUTCOME leaves missing or uncertain accounting untouched. VERIFY_OUTPUTS means scheduler completion alone did not establish that required outputs are valid, so the row remains unchanged. Other records are UNCHANGED. Neither reconciliation mode submits or cancels jobs. Unlike the scoped automatic gate, this manual operation reviews the project’s active tracked jobs.

Unknown legacy states and FAILED_BY_EXT allocations without confirmed termination are included. A dependency-blocked status describes logical work, not whether the scheduler has stopped the allocation. Reconciliation records confirmed failure/cancellation in scheduler_terminal_state while retaining FAILED_BY_EXT; run-based retries still require include_blocked = TRUE for that work. Legacy missing session metadata is treated as potentially overlapping a requested session, not as permission to launch another job.

Resolve one uncertain acceptance

Find the exact attempt, not just the participant or a row position:

diagnosis <- diagnose_project(scfg, interactive = FALSE)
diagnosis$submission_issues
attempts <- inspect_project(scfg)$submissions
contract_id <- "REPLACE_WITH_EXACT_CONTRACT_UUID"
attempt <- attempts[attempts$contract_id == contract_id, , drop = FALSE]
attempt

Review the attempt’s run, stage, subject/session, submission detail, manifest, and saved scheduler stdout/stderr under the run directory. Match scheduler accounting or administrator evidence to that exact attempt. If acceptance is confirmed, bind its allocation:

resolve_project_submission(scfg, contract_id, scheduler_job_id = "12345")

Alternatively, only if authoritative evidence establishes that no job was accepted, record that rejection instead:

resolve_project_submission(
  scfg, contract_id,
  rejection_reason = "Scheduler administrator confirmed this exact request was rejected."
)

These are mutually exclusive alternatives, not consecutive steps. Supply exactly one of scheduler_job_id and rejection_reason. This function has no dry-run mode: it updates the database immediately and preserves the recorded evidence. Binding retains worker-reported state; it does not verify outputs or make an active allocation safe to duplicate. Rejection is allowed only for unbound UNKNOWN or SUBMITTING attempts.

Queue absence, elapsed time, and missing logs are not evidence of rejection. If the outcome cannot be confirmed, leave the attempt unresolved and seek scheduler support rather than deleting tracking rows or starting in a new directory to evade the guard. Keep the configured log directory’s runs/ tree together with SQLite when backing up or moving a project.

Keep input and environment problems separate

A BIDS-root heudiconv.lock blocks relevant work. BrainGnomes does not remove it automatically: confirm whether conversion is still active and investigate the lock before any manual cleanup. For input problems, finish conversion, run run_bids_validation() separately, and review its report before launching preprocessing. Changing output directories does not repair shared BIDS inputs; do not rename or delete anatomical acquisitions just to silence validation.

doctor_project() is an optional, read-only environment and recovery-evidence review. It can help diagnose changed modules, permissions, containers, or missing records, but neither replaces the automatic submission gate nor performs either recovery action.

Inspect run provenance

Before deciding what to rerun, inspect the settings and scope that produced the selected run:

provenance <- get_run_provenance(scfg, run_id)
provenance$request
provenance$execution$subjects
provenance$configuration$snapshot_file
provenance$submission_preflight

The provenance bundle records the resolved stages and subjects, configuration, resources, software, host, and fingerprints of execution-driving files.

Retry failed work after correcting the cause

Resolve uncertain acceptance before deciding what to rerun. A submission that never acquired a tracked job may not appear in a run-based retry plan; after confirming rejection and fixing its cause, repeat the intended run_project() request. Use the run-based retry below for recorded failed or cancelled work.

A retry creates a new run. It does not restart scheduler jobs in place and does not change the original run. Always preview it first:

retry_plan <- retry_project_run(scfg, run_id, dry_run = TRUE)
retry_plan$jobs
retry_plan$subjects

After correcting the underlying cause, submit the retry explicitly:

retry_run <- retry_project_run(scfg, run_id, dry_run = FALSE)

Jobs marked FAILED_BY_EXT were blocked by an earlier failure and are excluded by default. Include them when appropriate:

retry_plan <- retry_project_run(
  scfg, run_id, include_blocked = TRUE, dry_run = TRUE
)

Cancel work that is still active

Cancellation targets outstanding tracked allocations, including unconfirmed dependency-blocked jobs that may still be queued or running. It does not delete data, logs, or completed outputs. Preview the scheduler commands before making a separate explicit cancellation request:

cancel_project_run(scfg, run_id, dry_run = TRUE)
cancel_project_run(scfg, run_id, dry_run = FALSE)

A successful cancellation command returns cancellation_requested, not cancelled: acknowledgement does not prove all allocation processes have stopped. SQLite remains unchanged, preserving any concurrent worker completion. Use a refreshed inspection to observe progress, then preview/apply reconcile_project_jobs() once accounting confirms failure or cancellation. The next relevant live run_project() performs this reconciliation automatically. Missing accounting or a still-active allocation continues to block a duplicate launch; a cancellation request itself never bypasses the gate.

Command-line inspection and recovery

The command line exposes the same inspection resolutions:

# Replace this value with the run ID reported by BrainGnomes status.
run_id="REPLACE_WITH_RUN_ID"
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study --view=stages
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study --view=subjects
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study --sub-id=540294
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study --view=active --refresh
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study --view=reconciliation
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study --run=latest --watch
BrainGnomes status /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --view=jobs --format=csv

BrainGnomes diagnose /project/my_study
BrainGnomes diagnose /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --interactive
BrainGnomes diagnose /project/my_study --subject-id=540294 --interactive
BrainGnomes diagnose /project/my_study --job-id=66273010 --interactive
BrainGnomes logs /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --failed-only --tail=50
BrainGnomes provenance /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --format=json

BrainGnomes retry /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --dry-run
BrainGnomes retry /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --yes
BrainGnomes cancel /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --dry-run
BrainGnomes cancel /project/my_study --run="$run_id" --yes

Retry and cancellation require either a dry-run preview or explicit confirmation. Neither routine inspection nor diagnosis changes scheduler state. The two explicit reconciliation/resolution functions above are R APIs; this guide does not require separate CLI recovery subcommands.
